speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The first set of amendments is to implement transparency-related changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Obligations similar to those required of companies will apply to LLPs, recipients of notices from LLPs and their controllers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Minister will also be empowered to direct the Registrar to maintain a central register of controllers of LLPs in the event a central register becomes a new internationally-agreed standard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Besides the register of controllers, the LLP Act will be amended to implement three changes on record retention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, not to allow an LLP that is wound up by its partners or creditors to destroy records early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such an LLP will have to retain its records for at least five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, to require former partners or managers of an LLP that has been struck off and dissolved to retain its accounting records and registers of controllers for at least five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) will publish guidance to help LLPs comply with the new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The final set of amendments will remove the requirement for a common seal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With the change, LLPs can execute documents by having them signed by two partners of an LLP, or a partner of an LLP in the presence of a witness who attests the signature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Notwithstanding the change, LLPs can choose to retain the use of a common seal based on business needs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill allows our businesses to continue operating with minimal costs while adhering to statutory requirements and ensures that our regulatory regime keeps up with the times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note that a public consultation on the proposed changes for companies and LLPs was held via the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH) as the Senior Minister of State just mentioned.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A detailed summary of feedback received was also published online, and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) and ACRA even went as far as to publish the corresponding responses to each category of feedback.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This high level of stakeholder engagement is a welcome initiative and I would like to commend this effort.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am also heartened by the fact that many of the proposals from the public were taken into serious consideration, resulting in some amendments to the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I mentioned in my Budget speech, I believe there is merit in greater engagement with stakeholders before the proposal of each Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should always listen to feedback, spot gaps and co-develop solutions with the community.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a positive step to reduce auxiliary costs of doing business in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, we are able to use cheaper alternative methods, such as electronic signatures sent with official emails, to ensure the authenticity of documents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Moving forward, I would like to ask if the Ministry would be conducting a thorough review to identify and subsequently remove similar non-essential costs when incorporating businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, will ACRA be doing another round of review to streamline regulatory fee structure?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Considering that the last review was done more than two years ago, it would be timely to conduct another one soon.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will go a long way in supporting entrepreneurs and startups, as they can then allocate resources to essential needs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will improve transparency and enhance confidence in our regulatory environment, as creditors, accountants and other stakeholders will have a longer period of access to key business documents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also applaud the removal of the option for LLPs to destroy records early if they are wound up by partners or creditors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This prevents the destruction of potential evidence of fraudulent business practices.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, a longer period of retention will result in higher costs of storage for businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The cost will have to be borne by the owners of the businesses and it is important to ensure that it is kept within reasonable limits.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The higher costs could also mean that when company assets are rounded up, creditors end up with less, which might be unfair to them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this regard, is the Ministry exploring more cost-effective means of technology to ensure the retention of key documents of the wound-up LLPs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, as I raised earlier in the Companies (Amendment) Bill, why is the retention period increased to five years?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I note again that the retention of books and papers after a company has been struck off, we are similarly increasing that period to five years.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would also like to thank the respondents who took part in the engagement for their useful feedback.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Louis Ng's first question is whether MOF will conduct a thorough review about our corporate regulations to remove unnecessary costs for the business community.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Apart from reviewing the laws, MOF and ACRA also review ACRA's regulatory fees every few years.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will continue to monitor areas where we keep business costs reasonable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the second issue of record retention, Mr Louis Ng has asked whether MOF is exploring most cost-effective means of technology for retaining records of wound -up LLPs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Liquidators of wound-up LLPs will have the flexibility to decide how the records should be kept.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The law does not prescribe the format for keeping records.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The business community should explore and adopt the most cost-effective means to keep their records.
